task.description: WF-03 Step 4 coverage-verification pass on ELIXIR-DEV's already-written ISS-0397 test coverage (REVIEWER PASS at Step 3d). acceptance_criteria: Design doc §5.1-§5.4 each mapped to an actual test in the four target files

create/2's insert_instance_projection/8 extension confirmed to have its own, non-inherited test assertion
Test isolation (unique tenant fixtures, no shared mutable state) confirmed
Full targeted suite re-run with real, quoted output

coverage_mapping.design_5.1_serial_cross_call_happy_path: test/letflow/iss0397_join_counters_test.exs, describe 'serial cross-call join: complete_task/3 called twice, as two separate top-level invocations' -- matches design steps 1-3 exactly (create/2, first separate complete_task/3 on task_a asserting :active + partial cohort, second separate complete_task/3 on task_b asserting :completed + deleted cohort). Point 4 (negative-control note) satisfied via in-code comment (lines 192-201) rather than a live pre-fix re-run, per the design's own wording ('should note this... without needing to check out the pre-fix revision') -- and independently corroborated by this step's own mutation test below, which is a live re-derivation of exactly that negative control against the concurrent variant.
coverage_mapping.design_5.2_concurrent_task_async: test/letflow/iss0397_join_counters_test.exs, describe 'concurrent sibling-branch completion' -- real Task.async/await_many over two separate Postgres connections (provisioned_tenant! sets Sandbox.mode :auto), asserts exactly one :completed / one :active outcome, join_counters == %{} after both commit, both tasks :completed. This is the load-bearing test verified by mutation (see mutation_check below).
coverage_mapping.design_5.3_timer_fire_parity: test/letflow/engine/timer_wiring_test.exs, describe 'ISS-0397: a join cohort opened by complete_task/3 is durably closed by advance_after_timer_fired/3' -- HUMAN_TASK branch completes via a separate complete_task/3 call, TIMER branch fires via a separate Scheduler.poll_and_fire/1 call (re-entering advance_after_timer_fired/3), asserting the cross-function-pair persistence parity design doc §5.3 calls for.
coverage_mapping.design_5.4_codec_round_trip: test/letflow/engine/snapshot_writer_test.exs, describe 'ISS-0397 -- serialize_join_counters/1 / deserialize_join_counters/1 round trip' -- pure single-process test round-tripping a non-empty JoinCounter map (all three MapSet fields populated) plus a separate empty-map edge case. Correctly placed in the existing SnapshotWriter test file per the design's stated preference against duplicate test files.
coverage_mapping.req208_meridian_test.exs: Both previously-broken scenario tests (loan-origination-above/below-threshold) updated to assert the now-successful second, separate complete_task/3 call instead of the pre-fix HTTP 500 -- confirmed via `git diff origin/main...HEAD` that the old CRITICAL FINDING moduledoc section was replaced with a 'FIXED by ISS-0397' section preserving the original defect's history rather than erasing it, and both test names/bodies changed from 'reproduces the join_counters defect (real HTTP 500)' to 'now advances the join cohort (ISS-0397)'.

mutation_check.target: lib/letflow/engine.ex, build_instance_state/3 (~line 1847): mutated `join_counters: SnapshotWriter.deserialize_join_counters(projection.join_counters)` back to the pre-fix hardcoded `join_counters: %{}`
mutation_check.method: In-place edit (not a worktree), per WF-03's 'apply in place, then git checkout --, verify' technique. mutation_check.mutant_result: 0/2 passed. Both the serial test and the concurrent test failed. The concurrent test's failure is the load-bearing evidence: `match (=) failed ... left: [branch_a: {:ok, _}, branch_b: {:ok, _}] ... right: [branch_a: {:error, {:activation_failed, {:unknown_branch_id, "<uuid>/0"}}}, branch_b: {:error, {:activation_failed, {:unknown_branch_id, "<uuid>/1"}}}]` -- this is the exact `{:unknown_branch_id, _}` failure mode the design doc's §1 and the test file's own comments predict for the pre-fix hardcoded `%{}`, reproduced live by this mutation, not merely asserted from documentation.
mutation_check.revert_verification: Reverted `build_instance_state/3`'s body to the original `join_counters: SnapshotWriter.deserialize_join_counters(projection.join_counters)` line. `git status --porcelain` returned EMPTY (confirmed via `git diff --stat lib/letflow/engine.ex` showing no output before revert-check and `git status --porcelain` after). Full targeted suite re-run post-revert: `mix test test/letflow/iss0397_join_counters_test.exs test/letflow/engine/timer_wiring_test.exs test/letflow/engine/snapshot_writer_test.exs test/letflow/simulation/req208_meridian_test.exs` -- Result: 36 passed, 0 failures.
mutation_check.note: This is a fix to pre-existing behavior (build_instance_state/3 already existed, just hardcoded a wrong value), not a case of 'the code under test did not exist' -- so the standard fail-then-pass rule applies (already satisfied by ELIXIR-DEV/REVIEWER's own prior runs) and this mutation is an independent re-derivation of that same evidence for this gate, not the WF-03 non-existence-exception procedure (which does not apply here).

create2_extension_coverage_check.verdict: PASS -- genuinely distinct, non-inherited coverage exists
create2_extension_coverage_check.finding: Confirmed by reading engine.ex directly (persist/12, ~line 965): create/2's Multi.run(:instance_projection, ...) step calls insert_instance_projection/8 with `new_instance_state.join_counters` as its 8th argument -- a write site distinct from reconcile_projection/5 (which every other write-site test in this suite exercises via complete_task/3 or advance_after_timer_fired/3). test/letflow/iss0397_join_counters_test.exs's serial test asserts `projection_after_create` (read immediately after Engine.create/2, before any complete_task call) has a join cohort with `expected_from_branches` length 2 and empty `received_from_branches` (lines 165-170) -- this is a direct assertion on insert_instance_projection/8's own write, not an assertion reachable only via reconcile_projection/5's later update. No gap found; no test change needed for this item.

test_isolation_check.finding: All four files use TenantFixture.provisioned_tenant!/1 (or the equivalent local insert_tenant!+provision_tenant_schema+replay_migrations sequence in snapshot_writer_test.exs) with a unique per-test-run slug/schema, each with its own on_exit teardown dropping the tenant schema. Definition names, idempotency keys, and actor_ids are all generated via System.unique_integer/1 or Ecto.UUID.generate/0 helpers (unique_name/1, unique_idempotency_key/1) -- no hardcoded ids shared across tests or across the concurrent Task.async pair. All four files declare `async: false` consistently (matching every other tenant-fixture-using file in this codebase), and the concurrent test explicitly sets Sandbox.mode :auto (not the default per-process :manual sandbox) so the two Task.async calls are a genuine cross-connection race, not artificially serialized by shared sandbox ownership. No shared mutable state found between tests or between files.
